structures.name: Arytenoid cartilage
structures.caption: Paired pyramid-shaped cartilages that sit on top of the cricoid. The vocal cords attach to them, and they pivot to open and close the airway.

facts.q: What type of cartilage makes up most of the arytenoid?

structures.name: Corniculate cartilage
structures.caption: Small horn-shaped caps on the tips of the arytenoids. Elastic cartilage.

facts.q: What type of cartilage is the corniculate cartilage?

structures.name: Cricoid cartilage
structures.caption: The only complete ring of cartilage in the airway. Seen from behind, this is its wide plate (lamina). Narrow in front, wide in back, like a signet ring.

facts.q: What type of cartilage is the cricoid cartilage?

structures.name: Trachealis muscle
structures.caption: Band of smooth muscle across the back of the trachea. It closes the gap in each C ring, so the back of the trachea is flat and soft where it rests against the esophagus.

facts.q: What type of tissue is the trachealis?

structures.name: Cuneiform cartilage
structures.caption: Small rod-shaped elastic cartilages inside the folds that run from the arytenoids up to the epiglottis. They stiffen those folds.

facts.q: What type of cartilage is the cuneiform cartilage?

structures.name: True vocal cords
structures.caption: Paired folds stretched between the thyroid cartilage in front and the arytenoids behind. The slit between them is the rima glottidis. Air passing between them makes sound.

facts.q: What is the opening between the true vocal cords called?
